transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. We need to get through the lock meeting before the Saturday 9 PM Eastern live finale. Per our standard process, I need each function — standards, platform production, rights, and data protection — to state their complete current finding, every exact requirement, and the corresponding change needed in the draft before I can close the voting package. Let's start with standards. Who's reporting?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Per the network's current standards memo — which was issued after the draft voting rules were circulated — I'm confirming three standards requirements: first, voters must be at least 13 years old; second, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account; third, voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. The current draft does not reflect any of these three requirements, so all three must be added before the package can be closed.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I completed the platform certification test this morning. The SMS integration failed certification, while the web portal passed. The approved portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted. This means the current draft's allowance of SMS voting must be removed, and the web portal with account verification must be the sole voting method.

transcript.text: Rights here. I obtained the finalist label's written approval today. The voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but may not use any finalist performance audio or video. The current draft interface still contains performance clips, so all finalist performance audio and video clips must be removed from the voting interface before the package can be closed.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Data protection here. My privacy review, completed with the voting vendor this week, produced two requirements: first, participation must be limited to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada; second, voter identifiers must be deleted within 30 days. The current draft still describes worldwide participation and has no deletion step, so both must be corrected before the package can be closed.
